newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai banker Thanong seen as new finance minister.
newsitem.headline: Thai banker Thanong seen as new finance minister.

text.p: Little-known banker Thanong Bidaya was set to take the hot-seat post of Thai finance minister after a number of top candidates for the difficult job turned it down, political sources and local media reports said on Friday.

The Bangkok Post quoted sources as saying the U.S.- and Japan-educated Thanong, currently president of Thai Military Bank, had been offered the job by Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, and he had accepted.
"He is a low profile banker and we don't know much about him, but he seems like a second- or third-rate choice," said an analyst at a foreign brokerage.

Former finance minister Amnuay Viravan quit abruptly on Thursday over political differences with rivals in Chavalit's six-party coalition government. His departure caused the stock and money markets to plunge.

Political sources told Reuters that as of Thursday afternoon, Thanong's name was still low on the list of candidates, which was topped by economic heavyweights such as Siam Commercial Bank President Olarn Chaiprawat and former cabinet minister Virabongsa Ramangkura.
But as prime candidates turned down offers for the difficult portfolio, the 50-year-old Thanong became the best choice left, they said.

"We have to overcome time constraints since the government needs to prepare for the Budget Bill debate next week," a source told the Bangkok Post. Parliament is set to debate the budget at a special June 25-27 session.

The Nation newspaper quoted political observers as saying the decision to pick Thanong "confirmed speculation that top economic thinkers were distancing themselves from the government or (were) too anxious about intense political plays to accept the big burden (of being finance minister)".
The Post, quoting a source close to the premier, said Thanong was chosen after Olarn turned the job down.

Analysts and sources from his own bank said that even though Thanong's background was less illustrious than that Amnuay, who has had a 38-year public career, he enjoyed a good relationship with the premier.
Chavalit had sought Thanong's advice on the economy from time to time, they said.
Thanong started at the Thai Military Bank as a mid-level manager and worked his way up the corporate ladder to become the bank's top executive in 1992.
He received his first degree in Japan and then moved to the United States where he received his masters and doctorate degrees in business administration at Northwestern University in Chicago.
Thailand has had five finance ministers in three governments since 1995 and is going through its worst economic slump in over a decade.

The ailing finance sector is in trouble with over-exposure to the depressed property sector, exports have turned sluggish, the stock market has plunged to eight-year lows and the baht has come under speculative attack.
Economic growth this year is seen at a more than 10-year low of 5.9 percent against 6.4 percent posted in 1996.
No official confirmation of Thanong's reported appointment was available from the prime minister's office.
